name: Gulliver Osei-Tarkhan
role: Independent vehicle mechanic specializing in Ferrogate Transit auxiliary vehicles and civilian cargo crawlers
location: Geartown, Ironvein sub-block, bay unit 7, near Milwaukee and Damen
description:
Gulliver is lean and grease-darkened in a way that feels permanent, as though the machine oil has become part of his pigmentation — his hands are always a shade darker than his forearms no matter how much he scrubs. He has his mother's Ghanaian cheekbones and his father's Kazakh jaw, which together give him a face that people find hard to stop looking at without knowing quite why. He keeps his hair close-cropped except for two finger-wide stripes he has dyed iridescent copper, a remnant of a decade-old fashion he never bothered to give up. He has a prehensile tail modification — mottled gray-brown with a slightly prehensile curl — that he got at nineteen and has used as a third utility limb ever since: it holds tools, hooks parts bins, and occasionally taps impatiently on the floor when he is thinking.

Gulliver is constitutionally incapable of leaving a broken thing alone. This is a professional gift and a personal curse. His bay is organized with the obsessive logic of a man who has lost a critical component one too many times and never forgot it. He is not unfriendly but he is focused, and conversations with him often drift sideways into the mechanics of whatever he happens to be working on. He keeps a small ELF shrine mounted above his main workbench — a figure he calls Grease Aunt, fashioned from fused capacitors and old gasket rings — and consults it before any job that involves a vehicle with a history of instability.

core_fears: losing the use of his hands
being trapped in obligation to someone powerful enough that he cannot refuse
core_desires: to work only on problems that genuinely interest him
to eventually open a second bay and hire one good apprentice
coping_mechanisms: hyperfocusing on mechanical problems to avoid emotional processing
physical humor and deflection when conversations get too personal
blind_spots: underestimates how much people notice and rely on him
takes on jobs he shouldn't out of compulsive curiosity about the machine
psychology.secret: He has been covertly maintaining a Ferrogate Transit emergency crawler that he rebuilt from scrap — it is not registered anywhere and he uses it occasionally to move people who need to get somewhere without being tracked, never charging them, telling himself it is just a test run

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical vocabulary bleeds into everything; uses mechanical metaphors constantly without noticing; drops into Twi occasionally when frustrated
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid when explaining something he knows well, halting and mid-sentence-stopping when trying to talk about feelings
verbal_tics: 'yeah, no, but—' as a way of agreeing and adding a complication simultaneously
trailing off in the middle of a sentence because he has started thinking about something else
example_lines: Yeah, no, but the thing is the thing you think is broken is never actually the thing that's broken — it's the thing two steps upstream from that. Always.
She runs fine until she doesn't. That's the job.

story_hooks: A vehicle brought in for routine work has a hidden smuggling compartment built into the chassis — the person who dropped it off hasn't come back for three days

Ferrogate Transit's auxiliary depot manager is pushing Gulliver to sign an exclusivity contract that would effectively make him a corporate employee; he is resisting but the financial pressure is real
narrative_function: Reliable repair and gear contact for anyone needing vehicle access or maintenance information; knows the Ferrogate Transit auxiliary fleet's unofficial quirks intimately; can identify vehicle origins and modifications; potential hook into Geartown criminal infrastructure through what he sees without asking
augmentations: Geneware prehensile tail (gray-brown, partial prehensility). Subdermal tool-link ports in left forearm for direct diagnostic handshake with vehicle systems. Iridescent copper hair stripes (pigment geneware, low-grade).
daily_life: Arrives at bay 7 by 07:30, runs diagnostic queues on anything left overnight, spends most of the day underneath or inside machines, eats a flatbread he buys from the cart outside while reviewing job lists, and often stays past midnight if something has him genuinely puzzled.
affiliation: Independent; informal contract relationships with Ferrogate Transit auxiliary depot

decision_rules: will not work on military hardware regardless of pay
always gets paid half upfront, no exceptions
escalation_ladder: blunt statement that the conversation is over
physical removal of himself from the situation — leaves the bay entirely

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally direct, not unfriendly, assesses whether they know anything about machines as a measure of compatibility
interpersonal_modes.friends: Relaxed, teasing, generous with time and knowledge

stress_responses.low: Works faster, becomes monologue-y about whatever he is doing
stress_responses.medium: Goes silent, tail curls tight, answers in single words
stress_responses.high: Abrupt and sharp-edged, liable to say something honest that he will regret

contradictions: Insists he only cares about machines and not people, then quietly fixes things for neighbors who haven't asked and can't pay
habits: taps his tail three times on the ground before starting any complex diagnostic
always knows what time it is without checking
breaking_points: being ordered to do something that will hurt someone who trusted him
watching someone mistreat a well-made machine

timeline.event: Started as a runner-fetch kid for a Geartown body shop at age 18
Earned his independent bay license after four years of apprenticeship under a mechanic who retired to Mexicantown Libre
Signed first informal contract with Ferrogate Transit auxiliary depot; has renewed it annually without committing to exclusivity
Completed the secret crawler rebuild; has used it six times
